title: The Jacobi-symbol conjecture for the integers $c_p$
source: Deyi Chen and Zhi-Wei Sun, “On determinants involving (j^2-k^2p) and (jkp)”, arXiv:2408.14401 (2024). (https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.14401), Conjecture 1.1

lanes.final_paper_definition_and_prior_art_che: final-paper-check-364499-opus-20261119-r1/CHECK-364499.md (Claude Opus 5.5, PASS WITH EDITORIAL EDITS; revised paper used)

significance.root_decision: For every odd prime p, the Jacobi symbol (p / c_p) equals 1, where c_p is the positive odd integer defined by the determinant identities of Chen and Sun (Theorem 1.1 of the source); existence and uniqueness of c_p are proved as part of the statement. This is Conjecture 1.1 of the source. Orientation matters: with c_p on top the symbol is -1 for 16 of the 80 odd primes up to 419. The proof uses a Vandermonde factorization, an integer skew-block identity for p = 1 mod 4, and a signed Pfaffian with its square identity and a character evaluation for p = 3 mod 4. Significance is low to modest (review 0.3).
significance.caveat: Low to modest significance (user may overrule). No citing papers were found; arXiv keyword search and Google Scholar could not be used, and some 2026 journal papers were read only through reference lists. Related work by Ren and Luo (arXiv:2407.04556) uses similar methods on other matrices.

root_basis: Root extracted all 35 modules from the appendix into an empty directory, rebuilt and kernel-checked them (all exit 0, object hashes identical to the author build, axioms exactly the allowed three), and screened the omega registry (its Chen-Sun notes are about a different paper). An independent Opus referee checked the Lean definitions against the source (literal or equivalent, orientation and non-vacuity confirmed), read the paper line by line, recomputed c_p and the symbol for all 80 odd primes up to 419, and did a further prior-art pass; its editorially revised copy is the accepted paper.
